observation.visible_scene: A hydraulic press with a cylindrical steel platen is positioned above a vertical stack of bricks resting on a yellow-and-black striped cylindrical base, surrounded by a pile of brick rubble. A GoPro camera on a mount and striped safety poles frame the left and right edges against a gray machine housing. The stack, from bottom to top, consists of a dark brick, two reddish bricks, and a top dark brick contacting the platen.
visible_changes: The platen descends steadily and continuously onto the top dark brick throughout the excerpt, shortening the overall stack height.
For the first several frames (up to about frame 13) the bricks remain visually intact with no new cracks.
A vertical crack appears in the upper reddish brick (around frame 14), then a crack forms in the lower reddish brick (around frame 15), accompanied by dust puffs.
The two reddish bricks progressively split into fragments; pieces detach, fall downward, and eject sideways off the stack, producing visible dust clouds.
The middle of the stack collapses into rubble, leaving the top dark brick supported only by a thin column of crushed debris as the platen keeps pressing it down.
Fragments and dust accumulate on the striped base and on the surrounding rubble pile, while the background poles, camera mount, and housing remain fixed.
The source of the press's force and whether it will retract after this segment are unseen.
The stack already shows prior crushing (rough top brick, surrounding debris) before this crop, so earlier loading history is unknown.
The final resting state of the fragments and the maximum load reached are not shown.
Exact material identities of the bricks are inferred only from appearance.
The precise moment of first cracking is approximate due to frame sampling.
Some small flying fragments may be motion-blurred, making it hard to distinguish separate pieces from dust.
